title: UN Fund Seeks $600 Million So Crisis-Hit Children Can Keep Learning
title_zh: 联合国教育基金筹资六亿美元，助力危机中的儿童继续上学
source_name: UN News — “UN News Today 02 November 2026” (Education Cannot Wait appeal); ECW “Hope Starts Here”
summary_zh: 全球基金 Education Cannot Wait（教育不能等）正发起约六亿美元筹资，目标在未来四年再帮助一千万受冲突与气候冲击影响的儿童继续接受安全、优质的教育；其中至少一半为女童，并计划覆盖一百万残疾儿童。日内瓦高级别认捐会定于2026年11月5日举行。本文适合积累教育、人道主义援助与国际合作类雅思词汇。
paragraphs: Across 87 countries, nearly 260 million school-aged children and teenagers have had their education disrupted by emergencies such as conflict and climate shocks. According to the United Nations, about 93 million of them are entirely out of school today, and eight in ten of those out-of-school children live in just 20 countries. For many families, classrooms, books and trained teachers feel further away than ever.

To confront this gap, Education Cannot Wait (ECW) — the UN global fund for education in crises — is seeking about 600 million US dollars. The money would support both rapid emergency response and longer-term investment in schooling and recovery between 2027 and 2030. With full funding, the fund aims to reach 10 million more children and adolescents with safe, inclusive and quality education. At least half of those reached would be girls, and one million would be children with disabilities.

A High-Level Replenishment Conference in Geneva on 5 November 2026, hosted by Switzerland, is the key moment for governments and partners to pledge. Early commitments from countries including Germany, the United Kingdom and Switzerland have already secured close to 40 per cent of the target — roughly 284 million dollars so far. Organisers say every new pledge signals that the world will not give up on a generation whose future depends on learning.

The campaign, known as Hope Starts Here, comes at a difficult time for aid. Global support for education is under pressure, and education in emergencies often receives only a small share of humanitarian budgets. ECW argues that when schools close, children lose not only lessons but also protection, routine and access to other services. Keeping learning going is both a right and a practical way to rebuild communities after crisis.

Over the past decade, ECW and its partners say they have already reached more than 14 million crisis-affected learners. The fund typically responds to new emergencies within about eight weeks, keeps overheads low, and plans to channel at least half of its financing to local and national partners by 2030.

For IELTS learners, this story links education, inequality and international cooperation. Notice how the text moves from the scale of the problem to concrete goals — funding targets, girls and children with disabilities — and then to a call for action. Similar problem–solution and cause–effect patterns often appear in Reading passages and in Writing Task 2 essays on education and development.
paragraphs_zh: 在87个国家里，近2.6亿学龄儿童和青少年的教育因冲突、气候冲击等紧急情况而中断。据联合国称，其中约9300万人目前完全失学，而这些失学儿童中有八成生活在仅20个国家。对许多家庭来说，教室、课本和受过训练的教师比以往任何时候都显得更加遥远。
为填补这一缺口，联合国危机教育全球基金 Education Cannot Wait（ECW，「教育不能等」）正在寻求约6亿美元资金。这笔钱将用于支持快速应急响应，以及2027至2030年间对学校教育与灾后恢复的长期投入。若资金到位，该基金计划再帮助1000万儿童和青少年获得安全、包容且优质的教育。其中至少一半将是女童，另有100万为残疾儿童。
定于2026年11月5日在日内瓦举行、由瑞士主办的高级别认捐会议，是各国政府与合作伙伴作出承诺的关键节点。包括德国、英国和瑞士在内的国家已提前认捐，目前已筹集到目标金额近四成——约2.84亿美元。组织方表示，每一笔新的认捐都表明：世界不会放弃这一代人的未来，而他们的未来取决于学习。
这场名为「希望从这里开始」（Hope Starts Here）的运动，恰逢援助形势艰难之时。全球对教育的支持承压，紧急情况下的教育在人道主义预算中往往只占很小份额。ECW认为，学校一旦关闭，儿童失去的不仅是功课，还有保护、日常秩序以及获得其他服务的机会。让学习持续下去既是一项权利，也是危机后重建社区的切实途径。
ECW及其合作伙伴表示，过去十年他们已帮助逾1400万受危机影响的学习者。该基金通常在约八周内对新发紧急情况作出响应，管理费用保持较低，并计划到2030年将至少一半资金导向地方和国家合作伙伴。
对雅思学习者来说，这篇报道把教育、不平等与国际合作联系在一起。注意文章如何从问题的规模转向具体目标——筹资目标、女童与残疾儿童——再到行动呼吁。类似的「问题—解决」和「因果」展开方式，常出现在阅读文章以及教育与发展类写作任务二中。
